 Everton are under the lights on Sky Sports for the second time in a week following Monday’s 1-0 win at Newcastle United, this time for a home fixture against Coventry City at the Hill Dickinson Stadium (kick-off, 8pm).
 The hosts are going along nicely and should fancy their chances against a Sky Blues side hovering just above the drop zone. I have a few football betting tips for this one, with all the info below.

 Toffees look too tough for Coventry
 Both sides will be heading into this fixture happy with recent results, but it’s Everton I fancy to come out on top at the Hill Dickinson tonight.
 After nearly quarter of the league season, the Toffees sit seventh, eyeing a European spot and also  enjoying a good run in the EFL Cup .
 There’s plenty to be positive about, then, for David Moyes and his players, and they should have too much for a Coventry side who have been all or nothing so far.
 Like Everton, Frank Lampard’s team have three league wins this term but they have lost their other six matches, whereas their opponents tonight have drawn four and lost only twice.
 Coventry’s three wins have all come in their last five fixtures, but they ‘lost’ the xG (expected goals) count in all of those games, including last week’s 3-1 home win over Sunderland.
 Everton were good value for their 1-0 win at Newcastle on Monday night and this is a game they should be winning at home, where they have two wins and a draw from four league games this term.
 Moyes has seen his side beaten only twice in 12 games in all competitions this season, both times by a 2-0 scoreline against both a potent  Chelsea at home and  away to champions Arsenal . And Coventry don’t have the same firepower as those sides.
 Everton are odds-on but don’t look a bad price so I’m keeping my first recommendation simple and that’s for the hosts to claim all three points.
 Selection: Everton to win – 7/10
 Barry to find the back of the net
 Two of Everton’s standout performers this term have been striker Thierno Barry and playmaker Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall, and they are my focus in the player markets.
 Dewsbury-Hall can be backed at 21/20 with Betfred for a goal or an assist. The 28-year-old has scored two and laid on one in the league this season.
 Everton are likely to dominate possession and Dewsbury-Hall should be central to their productivity, having created six big chances in the league already this term.
 At bigger odds of 6/5, there is also Barry simply to score. He has four league goals in this campaign and should have had more.
 The 24-year-old Frenchman has missed a hatful of chances and, at 13 per cent, his goal-conversion rate from the number of shots taken is the lowest of the division’s top 11 scorers.
 However, it bodes well that he keeps putting himself in the right position and getting on the end of opportunities, and the most tempting option of all is the 4/1 about Barry to score first, which is much bigger odds than the first two prices mentioned.
 Everton are favourites to win this match but it may not be a high-scoring affair – more on that below – and Barry is the most likely to find an opening.
 Selection: First goalscorer – Thierno Barry – 4/1
 Everton duo underpin bet builder
 I’m putting a home win in my bet builder, the case for this already having been spelled out above.
 Next, I’m continuing my focus on Everton’s Barry and Dewsbury-Hall. The first-named is averaging over three shots a game in the league this season, so I’ll take him to have two or more shots tonight.
 And I’m including Dewsbury-Hall to have one or more shots – he’s averaging 2.6 shots in the division. They seem like reasonable suggestions in a game for which Everton are odds-on favourites.
 Finally, I’ll take under 4.5 goals. Everton haven’t conceded more than two goals in a game this season, while they haven’t scored more than two in a league fixture this term either.
 Coventry did put four past Newcastle last month and three past Sunderland last week, but both were home games and on neither occasion were they actually value for that many goals.
 Selection: Bet builder - Everton to win; Barry 2+ shots; Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall 1+ shot; under 4.5 goals – 1.36/1
